messages.subject: Problem with req$POST()
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm running into some issues with rApache and using the requests objects. The code works fine with the built-in Rook webserver, but the issue seems to be that I trigger a call to rewind() which isn't supported by rApacheInputStream. I AM able to access the POST global object directly, so that's working as a workaround for now, but it seems like the 'right way' is to use the Request object.

See below for reproducible example.

Thanks!
Evan

Sample request (default content-type is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, but I run into the same issue regardless of what I set the content type to):
curl -v -d 'data={"a":"blah"}' http://127.0.0.1:9293/myapp

And sample app looks like the following.

library(RJSONIO)

app <- function(env) {

    req <- Rook::Request$new(env)
    res <- Rook::Response$new()

    tryCatch (

      if (req$post()){
          data <- req$POST()[["data"]]
          jsonData <- fromJSON(data)
          res$write(toJSON(jsonData)
      },
      error = function(cond) {
        message <- c(cond)
        names(message) <- c("error")
        res$write(toJSON(message))
      },
      warning = function(cond) {
        message <- c(cond)
        names(message) <- c("warning")
        res$write(toJSON(message))
      }
    )
    res$finish()
}

messages.subject: how to decently exit execution
messages.body_plain:
I feel rather stupid, but I do not understand how to stop the execution of a rApache script. I test the GET parameters, and if they are not consistent, I want to quit with an error message on screen. But quit() or error() (setContentType and setStatus) causes server errors, without decent message. Of course an if(...) {.....} else{.....} works, but there must be a more simple way. In the documentation "custom error messages"are mentioned, but I do not understand this section.
Thank you very much
Frans

messages.subject: Re: how to decently exit execution
messages.body_plain:
Have a look at opencpu. Its builds on rapache, and automatically deals with all this stuff for you. E.g. you can just use stop() in your script and it will automatically return a http400 with the error message in the body.

messages.subject: Re: rApache and Persistent data
messages.body_plain:
Hi, you could use svSocket package to create an "R Server", to which your rhtml (or whatever) files brew()ed before going to the browser connect and get and set data.

Basically, you open an RSession (via terminal or RStudio) then run in it:

library(svSocket)
startSocketServer() # here you can specify the port, defaults to 8888

Then, the rest of the job is as easy as writing at the beginning of your rhtml files the following:

con <- socketConnection(host = "localhost", port = 8888, blocking = FALSE) # see ?evalServer for examples

doing so is like using .rhtml + RServer as PHP + MySQL.

However, there are some big differences:
PHP can store variables across different sessions or page requests. (like in Rook when is not deployed in rApache)
MySQL writes onto the disk. So you'll have to pay extra care when writing to the server to not lose data if the server crashes.

I hope that helps. I attached an example of what just said.

Michele

On Wednesday, 17 April 2013 19:40:36 UTC+1, Armando wrote:
> I'm developing a web-based application with rApache, RJSONIO and Dojo.  So far so good.  I'm using r scripts that receive POST data and return JSON.  I've decided to "keep it all on one page" and there are no page transitions.  Dojo works nicely for that.
>
> An area that I think could use a bit more elegance, is how persistent data is handled. At the moment, each script parses POST data for user/sessionid information, loads in rData files, performs the functions needed in the script and then saves the rData files, when they change. Is there a way to make this more transparent?  Sometimes I run into errors and the data is not saved when it would be nice if it was.
>
> Any thoughts or suggestions on what would be the best way to handle persistent data with rApache or is basically the technique I'm using the best way?  Databases can be used but they too must be called explicitly.  As far as I know, there is no way to keep persistent data without some explicit method in R.
>
> (I was thinking it might be a nice feature to have "pre" and "post" file handers or something like that, where scripts are executed before (pre) and after (post) any script that runs.  These could be used to load and save env data needed for the app.)
>
>
